metaDescription: Six garden sprayers for liquid fertilizer, from hose end dilution bottles to one gallon pump tanks, compared on mixing accuracy, spray pattern and rinse effort.
expertTake: The Chapin G390 is the pick for lawns and beds because a hose end sprayer mixes fertilizer as you spray and leaves no tank to clean. The Ortho Dial N Spray is the pick when you want a labelled ratio dial. Skip pump sprayers for big lawns, since a hose end bottle covers more ground per minute with no pumping at all.
introParagraphs: Feeding plants with liquid fertilizer is a dilution problem first and a spraying problem second. Concentrate has to be blended with water to a label rate, and the sprayer either does that blending as you go or holds a pre mixed batch in a tank.

Those two approaches suit different gardens. A hose end bottle meters concentrate into the water stream and suits lawns and large beds, while a pump tank gives exact batch control and suits precise foliar feeding. This guide compares both types.

products.name: Chapin G390 32 Ounce Hose End Sprayer for Fertilizer
products.description:
A hose end sprayer is the simplest way to feed a lawn. You fill the 32 ounce bottle with water soluble concentrate, screw it onto a garden hose, and the flowing water draws the concentrate through a metering orifice as you walk. There is no pump to work, no tank to carry and no mixing in a bucket.

The design is intentionally basic: a chemical resistant poly concentrate tank, a fingertip on off control and a universal hose fit that an optional quick connect accessory makes faster. It meters one ratio, set by the head, so it is the best match for a fertilizer whose label rate matches that head. Compared with the Ortho dial model you give up adjustability but gain a lighter, cheaper bottle.

Care is simple: after each use, run clean water through the bottle and head with the concentrate valve open until it comes out clear, then store with the cap off. The head has a small anti siphon and metering path that clogs if fertilizer dries in it, so never store it with product inside. A good habit is to pour the last of a fertilizer batch through the bottle with the cap on and the hose off, so the pickup tube draws the remaining concentrate and you do not leave a puddle at the bottom to dry into a plug.
products.bestFor: Feeding lawns and large beds quickly with water soluble fertilizer.
pros: No pumping and no mixing bucket
Lowest price tier in the lineup
cons: One ratio set by the head

products.name: Ortho Dial N Spray Hose End Sprayer, 14 dilution settings

specList.label: Uses
specList.value: Liquid fertilizer, weed and insect killer, fungicide

products.description:
Fourteen dilution settings turn this from a single purpose bottle into a general purpose feeder. You read the label rate for your product, turn the dial to the matching setting, and the head meters the right amount of concentrate into the hose flow. That makes it far more forgiving when you switch between fertilizers, fungicides and liquid weed killers.

Three spray patterns let you broadcast across a lawn or place a narrower pattern near edges. The ergonomic design is meant to reduce hand strain on longer passes. Against the Chapin G390 it adds the dial but costs more, and against the Chameleon it gives a more obvious dilution scale.

Dial settings are a guide, not a precision instrument: hose pressure, the thickness of the concentrate and the walking pace all change the real ratio. Always flush with clear water and rotate the dial through its settings while rinsing, because dried fertilizer gums the dial passage.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who switch between several products and want a labelled dial.
pros: Works with fertilizer and other liquids
cons: Dial ratios are approximate in practice
Dial passage clogs if not flushed

products.name: RL Flo-Master Chameleon 32 Ounce Hose End Sprayer
products.description:
The Chameleon gets its name from three patterns in one head: a fan for general areas, a shower for delicate plants and a stream for high places. Because a hose end sprayer takes its spray strength from the hose, the pattern switch is how you tailor the output without changing nozzles.

The 32 ounce bottle serves fertilizer, weed killers, fungicides and insect killers, and the listing stresses that it keeps your hands away from direct contact with the chemical. That feature is a safety point when you handle concentrate. Compared with the Ortho you get patterns but no marked dilution dial, so it is better when your fertilizer label gives a simple mixing ratio that the head already matches.

Expect to rinse thoroughly after each use. If you spray weed killer through it, keep it for that job only, because residue is hard to purge and will burn lawn feed targets. For fertilizer only use, it is a durable, plain bottle. Because the head switches patterns by a twist collar, rinse that collar with the bottle running in each position, or the shower setting can lock up when a crust forms in the pattern ring.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who feed lawns, shrubs and tall plants with one head.
cons: Do not share it with herbicide

products.name: Humboldts Secret Hose End Sprayer 32 Ounce, 2 pack, 100:1
products.description:
Two bottles in the pack is the practical hook. You can dedicate one to fertilizer and another to a pest or fungicide product, which avoids cross contamination. Each bottle has a K1 head with a 100 to 1 mixing ratio, meaning roughly one part concentrate to a hundred parts water, which is a very dilute mix suited to light feeding.

That ratio is important for fertilizer: it tells you the head will not deliver a strong dose of concentrate. If your label asks for a heavier rate, a lower ratio head or a pump tank is a better match. The K1 head is a simple design with few parts.

Treat the two bottles as dedicated tools. Label each with a permanent marker, flush after every use, and store them with caps off. Since the K1 style heads have only a few parts, a blocked metering orifice can usually be cleared with warm water and a soft toothpick, which is cheaper than replacing the bottle. Where the Chapin G390 has one, this gives you two heads and a defined ratio, but you lose the quick connect option the Chapin mentions.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who want separate dedicated bottles for feed and pest products.
pros: Two bottles in a single pack
Simple K1 head with few parts
cons: Ratio is fixed, so heavy feeds do not suit

products.name: Chapin 20004 1 Gallon Pump Sprayer, funnel top tank
products.description:
When you want an exact, measured batch of liquid feed, a pump tank is more controllable than a hose end bottle. You mix a known amount of concentrate with a known volume of water, fill the one gallon tank, pump it up and spray. The result is a rate you can calculate instead of a rate the hose pressure decides.

The funnel top fills without splashing and the translucent tank lets you read the level. An anti clog filter protects the nozzle from undissolved particles. Compared with a hose end sprayer you need a bucket for mixing and a few minutes of pumping, but you also reach plants far from a tap.

Rinse the tank, filter and nozzle thoroughly after fertilizer because dried salts crust the pump head. A seal kit is inexpensive, and the tank is cheap enough to dedicate to feed only.
products.bestFor: Precise foliar feeding in beds and containers away from a tap.
pros: Cheap enough to dedicate to feed
cons: Pressure fades as the tank empties

products.name: PetraTools HD101 1 Gallon Pump Sprayer, 52 in hose
products.description:
This pump sprayer gets its edge for fertilizer from the long 52 inch hose and the second nozzle. A fine mist tip suits foliar feeding on leaves, and the adjustable one handles a drench around roots. With the tank on the ground, you can feed under shrubs without hoisting the whole weight.

The built in pressure release valve vents the tank before you open it, which matters when a feed mix is sitting in the tank under pressure. A translucent tank with a funnel shaped opening makes measuring and mixing quick. Compared with the Chapin 20004 you get better reach and safety, and compared with a hose end bottle you get exact batch control.

Rinse after every feed, especially around the nozzle where salts collect. Hang the hose loosely and keep a spare tip handy. When feeding in bright sun, spray in the morning or late afternoon so leaves can dry before the heat arrives, because wet foliage with dissolved salts is what scorches.
products.bestFor: Foliar feeding around shrubs and raised beds with a measured mix.
pros: 52 inch hose keeps the tank on the ground
Two nozzles for mist and drench
Funnel shaped opening for easy mixing
cons: Needs pumping and a mixing step
More hose to coil and store

buyingCriteria.explanation: A hose end sprayer like the Chapin G390 meters concentrate as water flows, so it is fast for lawns but its ratio depends on hose pressure. A pump tank like the Chapin 20004 sprays a mix you measured yourself, which is more exact but slower. Choose by whether speed or precision matters more to you.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Dilution ratio and the label rate
buyingCriteria.explanation: Fertilizer labels give a rate such as ounces per gallon or per 1,000 square feet. A 100 to 1 head like the Humboldts Secret delivers a very dilute mix, while the Ortho Dial N Spray offers 14 settings. Check that the head can reach the rate your label asks for before you buy.

A flat fan puts feed down evenly on turf, a shower is gentler on leaves and a stream reaches high or distant targets. The Chameleon bundles three patterns in one head and the Ortho dial lists three as well. Uneven patterns leave stripes of burned or hungry turf.

Hose end sprayers depend on the pressure and flow of your tap. Low pressure under-doses and high pressure can over-dose, which is why feed should be applied in measured passes. A pump tank like the PetraTools HD101 is independent of the tap, which helps in gardens with weak supply.

Fertilizer salts dry into a crust that clogs the metering path in a hose end head and the nozzle of a pump tank. Rinse right after use. Dedicated bottles, like the two pack Humboldts Secret, prevent carry over between products.

A hose end bottle is only as mobile as your hose, while a pump tank travels anywhere. The PetraTools HD101 with its 52 inch hose can feed plants in an outbuilding. Match the sprayer to where your plants are, not just to how big the lawn is.

specDecoder.meaning: The ratio of water to concentrate delivered by a hose end head, such as 100 to 1. A larger first number means a weaker mix.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Humboldts Secret lists 100 to 1, a light feeding ratio.

specDecoder.meaning: Dial positions on a hose end sprayer that change the rate of concentrate drawn in.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Ortho lists 14 settings, and the Chapin G390 does not list a dial.

specDecoder.meaning: The volume of concentrate or mix the bottle or tank holds.
specDecoder.watchFor: Hose end bottles hold 32 ounces of concentrate, but the Chapin 20004 holds a full gallon of mixed liquid.

specDecoder.meaning: The shape of the spray, from a flat fan to a stream.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Chameleon lists fan, shower and stream, which suits several tasks.

specDecoder.meaning: How the bottle attaches to a hose. A universal fit works with standard garden hose threads.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Chapin G390 lists a universal fit with an optional quick connect.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mixing accuracy
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated hose end heads with a fixed ratio from dial designs and from pump tanks that give an exact batch. The pump tanks scored highest for accuracy and the dial models for flexibility.

howWeEvaluated.title: Speed and coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how much ground each sprayer covers per fill. A 32 ounce hose end bottle can feed a lawn quickly, while a one gallon pump tank needs refills.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pattern and control
howWeEvaluated.description: Spray patterns and on off controls were compared. The Chameleon with three patterns and the Ortho with three scored well.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning burden
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on owner feedback patterns, clogged heads are the common complaint. We credited designs with simple heads and easy flushing.

howWeEvaluated.title: Product flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: Whether a unit suits fertilizer only or also other liquids was considered. The Ortho and Chameleon list multiple product types, while the two pack allows dedicated use.

rows: Beds and shrubs with mixed heights
Separate bottles for feed and pests

cards.label: Hose end sprayer
cards.text: Fast, no pumping, no mixing bucket, but the real rate depends on tap pressure. Picks: Chapin G390, Ortho Dial N Spray, RL Flo-Master Chameleon and Humboldts Secret.

cards.label: Pump tank
cards.text: A measured batch and independence from the tap, at the cost of pumping and refills. Picks: Chapin 20004 and PetraTools HD101.

howToChoose.note: Choose hose end for lawns near a tap, and a pump tank for precise foliar feeding.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A broad fan pattern, steady hose pressure and a head matched to the label rate. Walk at a steady pace with overlapping passes.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Chapin G390 is the fastest way to cover turf, and the Ortho dial lets you match different feeds. Use a pump tank for spot corrections.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You use several products or want the safety of a relief valve. The Ortho and PetraTools HD101 add control.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You feed a lawn once or twice a season. The Chapin G390 does that for the least money.

maintenance.task: Flush the head with clean water
maintenance.why: Fertilizer dries in the metering path and blocks it. Run water through the head until it is clear.
A dial passage left on one setting can seize. Moving it through all settings clears residue.
A cracked hose washer leaks at the connection. Replacements are cheap and a minute to fit.
Mixing up a herbicide bottle with a fertilizer bottle can kill a lawn. A permanent marker label prevents it.

maintenance.task: Store dry with the cap off
maintenance.why: Closed damp bottles grow mildew and block passages. Open storage keeps them clean.

faq.q: Is a hose end sprayer accurate enough for fertilizer?
faq.a: It is accurate enough for lawns if you follow the label and keep a steady pace. The real ratio varies with tap pressure, so avoid heavy feeds and walk in overlapping passes.

faq.q: What does a 100 to 1 ratio mean?
faq.a: It means roughly one part concentrate to a hundred parts water, a very dilute mix. Make sure the head can deliver the rate your label asks for.

faq.q: Can I use a hose end sprayer for weed killer and fertilizer?
faq.a: It is safer to keep separate bottles. Residue from weed killer can damage plants you later feed, so a two pack helps.

faq.q: Why does my hose end sprayer stop drawing liquid?
faq.a: The metering path or the pickup tube is usually clogged by dried fertilizer. Soak the head in warm water, flush it and clear the tube.

faq.q: Is a pump sprayer better for fertilizer?
faq.a: It gives an exact batch and does not depend on tap pressure, but it takes mixing and pumping. For big lawns near a tap, hose end is faster.

faq.q: How often should I feed with liquid fertilizer?
faq.a: Follow the product label, which usually specifies intervals in weeks. More is not better, because over feeding burns roots.
